title: ‘Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse’ Trailer Leaks Online, Prompting Co-Writer Chris Miller to Speak Out: ‘Not a Fan of Leaks of Unfinished Footage’
description:
“Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse” is the latest movie to get hit by an unauthorized leak.

	The trailer for the third “Spider-Verse” movie, whic
body:
“Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse” is the latest movie to get hit by an unauthorized leak.

	The trailer for the third “Spider-Verse” movie, which is scheduled to hit theaters on June 18, 2027, appeared to leak online on Twitter/X this week. Co-writer and producer Chris Miller disavowed the leak on Friday, writing “Not a fan of unfinished, not fully rendered footage.”

Not a fan of leaks of unfinished, not fully rendered footage— Christopher Miller (@chrizmillr) August 14, 2026


	“Beyond the Spider-Verse” is the latest high-profile movie to suffer a leak. This past month, billion-dollar blockbusters “The Odyssey” and “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” both leaked onto X after their theatrical releases. This is far from the first time a “Spider-Man” movie has been targeted; the trailer for 2021’s “Spider-Man: No Way Home” had also leaked weeks before debuting publicly online.
	

	Earlier this year, the full version of “Avatar Aang: The Last Airbender” also leaked onto X months before its Paramount+ streaming release. A 26-year-old man was later arrested in Singapore for illegally accessing a media server and leaking the film. The “Avatar Aang” cast and original “Last Airbender” stars soon spoke out against the breach and urged fans to not watch the unauthorized version.


	“There’s something about respecting the intentions of the creators and many artists who poured years of their life into this. To go about it the proper way is a very respectful way of showing appreciation to the art form and to the many, many, countless hours put into this,” star Eric Nam told Variety at Comic-Con after the leak. “Thank you guys for waiting.”
	

	After several delays, “Beyond the Spider-Verse” will wrap up Miles Morales’ story as Spider-Man. The first footage was shown exclusively at CinemaCon earlier this year

schema.headline: ‘Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse’ Trailer Leaks Online, Prompting Co-Writer Chris Miller to Speak Out: ‘Not a Fan of Leaks of Unfinished Footage’

title: Kyle Chandler and Aaron Pierre Are Great ‘Lanterns’, but HBO’s DC Drama Is Overshadowed by Its Influences: TV Review
description: Of all the superheroes to give the gritty realism treatment, the Green Lantern is an odd choice. Tasked with enforcing intergalactic order with a ma
body:
Of all the superheroes to give the gritty realism treatment, the Green Lantern is an odd choice. Tasked with enforcing intergalactic order with a magic ring bestowed by a group of blue aliens (before the Na’avi, there were the Guardians), the character occupies the opposite end of the tonal spectrum from Bruce Wayne stalking the streets of Gotham City sans powers. The larger DC Universe, as creatively overseen by the filmmaker James Gunn, already skews in a goofier, more cartoonish direction that embraces the inherent silliness of classic comics; last year’s “Superman” featured an appearance by a Green Lantern, Nathan Fillion’s Guy Gardner, as de facto comic relief, with an atrocious bowl cut to match.
	

	But the HBO drama “Lanterns” is just that: an HBO drama. And while the prestigious network has made some concessions to our current era of IP, airing multiple “Game of Thrones” spinoffs and prior DC productions like “The Penguin,” there are still limits in place. “Peacemaker,” a Gunn-led series that fits squarely within the producer’s established style, remains a product of online-only service HBO Max — a branding distinction that’s illegible to the average streaming subscriber but significant nonetheless.


	“Lanterns,” on the other hand, is an easily traceable composite of earlier HBO releases. Its wry humor and grounded fantasy recall “Watchmen,” the 2019 series that marked the platform’s initial toe dip into superhero stories; sure enough, “Watchmen” boss Damon Lindelof is one of three credited co-creators on “Lanterns.” The title characters, 2016-era Lantern Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) and his trainee John Stewart (Aaron Pierre), are mismatched partners in (space) law enforcement whose fraught relationship plays out over a split timeline, á la “True Detective.” Lo and behold, “Lanterns” co-creator and showrunner Chris Mundy worked on that anthology’s most recent season, as well as other crime shows (“Ozark,” the Chandler-starring “Bloodline”) known for a color palette as gloomy as their mood. (Frequent DC Comics writer Tom King completes the trifecta.)
	

	It’s of course common for comic book media to take inspiration from other genres, the way “WandaVision” paid homage to vintage sitcoms. Yet “Lanterns” is unusually direct in assembling its components, down to the typecasting of its leads. As the burnt-out Hal, an aging maverick forced to stare his own redundancy in the face, Chandler is back to playing a middle-aged mentor with folksy charm and a Texas twang. (Some of Hal’s pivotal scenes even play out on a high school football field, lest one miss the parallels to “Friday Night Lights.”) Pierre’s Stewart is taciturn, imposing and responds to an endless series of irritants with a steely reserve punctuated by bursts of controlled violence. That doubles as a description of Pierre’s breakout role in the action film “Rebel Ridge,” down to the premise of an ex-Marine spending time in an unfriendly small town against their will.

	This particular small town is Rushville, Nebraska, where Hal and John pause their bickering to investigate a shooting Hal’s gut tells him has an extraterrestrial element, putting the incident in the Lanterns’ jurisdiction. (Hal’s a big fan of vibes-based decisionmaking.) He’s right, much to the annoyance of local sheriff Kerry (Kelly Macdonald, back on HBO more than a decade after “Boardwalk Empire”), an exasperated woman with an accent just a few clicks to the left of Marge Gunderson. But “Lanterns” doesn’t bloom into Technicolor CGI when the aliens show up. 

	Instead, these visitors take on human form, including a Guardian who bears a striking resemblance to “Ozark” star Laura Linney. It’s part of a suite of aesthetic choices that keep “Lanterns” on Earth in more ways than one. Hal almost never wears his suit, a symptom of his disillusionment that also lets him sport a more understated brown jacket. He’s the first-ever human Lantern, but the only other ringbearer we meet is Hal’s disgraced mentor Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen), who could pass for homo sapiens apart from his pointy ears. Because John doesn’t wear the ring full-time yet, the pair has to accommodate his lack of flight and travel by car. (Though Hal likes to punk John by jumping out, leaving his younger companion to think fast or suffer the consequences.) There are flashes of the Lanterns’ typical terrain, like the flesh-eating plant Hal keeps for a pet, but they’re always brief.
	

	If “Lanterns” excises so much of what characterizes this corner of the DC Universe, then what exactly is the show’s interest in the Green Lantern? The answer turns out to be the nature of a position that’s assigned rather than assumed. There’s no external committee to decide whether Clark Kent deserves to be Superman; he simply is. Not so with the Lanterns, whose appointment by the Guardians raises all kinds of questions about worthiness and what really constitutes “earning” one’s ring. 

	This dual character study is where “Lanterns” is at its best. Chandler and Pierre may be squarely in their comfort zones, but that also puts them in a position to succeed. It’s especially gratifying to see Pierre fulfill the promise of the rising action star announced by “Rebel Ridge” after some detours into animation work and whatever “The Morning Show” is. An episode dedicated to John’s backstory, including a childhood raised by parents (Jasmine Cephas Jones and J. Alphonse Nicholson) obsessed with cultivating their own son into a perfect job candidate for the Guardians, is a highlight. Like “Watchmen,” “Lanterns” wants to consider the specific burdens and significance of the Black superhero. Its conclusions don’t land with the same force as its predecessor’s, but they’re also not positioned as a twist or reveal in the same way. Race is simply weaved into John’s reality alongside his talent for hand-drawing and passion for birds — particularly in how it feels to practice extreme self-discipline while forced to play second fiddle to an arrogant, less qualified white guy.

	Hal loves to tell the story of how he got the ring: a disembodied voice trapped him in a green bubble, asked if he was afraid and rewarded him when he said “no.” What “Lanterns” posits is that fearlessness — a quality John’s parents also worked to inculcate with horrifying, William Tell-style tests of his resolve — may not be an ideal quality to incentivize. By Hal’s own admission, his bravery comes from having nothing to lose. His dad, a fighter pilot, died when he was a child; one of the few nuggets of wisdom he offers John is not to form any meaningful relationships while he’s a Lantern. Much of Hal’s personality has been molded to fit Chandler’s distinct charisma, but the bitter edge feels new. What comes off as cavalier risk-taking is really a cover for something much more nihilistic.
	

	Pierre and Chandler do their best to banish the ghosts of Marty and Rust from the first season of “True Detective,” and even if they don’t entirely succeed (the many scenes of them squabbling on the road are just too direct a reference), they do give Hal and John a prickly and specific chemistry. The title “Lanterns,” plural, hints at the source of their tension. There’s only supposed to be one Green Lantern per planet at any given time, making John’s very presence in Hal’s life a personal affront he repays with the demanding nickname “Junior.” Whether John is Hal’s sidekick, deputy or replacement, the one thing he can’t be is a true partner.

	But this solid core is nested inside a less singular package. As the plot narrows into a search for a Manhunter, a murderous species whose vaunted ability to blend in is somewhat muted by every other alien having the same ability, each Lantern gets assigned a love interest. Hal flirts with Kerry; John has an affair with Zoe (Poorna Jagannathan), the wife of William Macon (Garret Dillahunt), a local cattle mogul whose compound has more high tech weaponry than a mere human would seem to need. Pierre and Jagannathan’s scenes have a charge enhanced by their characters’ age gap and frank conversations about navigating the overwhelmingly white Rushville. Kerry and Hal are the more perfunctory pairing, their connection more talked about than shown. Neither dalliance threatens the primacy of the true central relationship. 

	Watching “Lanterns,” you never escape the sense that the show is a piece of high-profile IP taking on the guise of a prestige drama, the way the Manhunter disguises itself among the cornfields. Not only is the show overt about its influences to the point where it can’t transcend them; it’s also a mix of shoe-leather investigation and glowing green lasers that never stops clashing. When Hal alludes to a planet of squirrels, it pierces the Rushville bubble of diners and motels. When the Guardians get in touch, you’re aware they have bigger fish to fry than our “galactic backwater.” At least there’s never long to wait until Chandler and Pierre are once again trading barbs, the place where “Lanterns” is most palpably in its preferred groove. 

	“Lanterns” will premiere on HBO and HBO Max on Aug. 16 at 9 p.m. ET, with remaining episodes airing weekly on Sundays.

schema.headline: Kyle Chandler and Aaron Pierre Are Great ‘Lanterns’, but HBO’s DC Drama Is Overshadowed by Its Influences: TV Review

title: Netflix Orders YA Gothic Romance ‘Sid & Zoey,’ Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Bad Robot to Produce
description:
In a competitive situation, Netflix has greenlit the YA romance series “Sid & Zoey.” 

	The show hails from creator Jon Kasdan and writer John Shiba
body:
In a competitive situation, Netflix has greenlit the YA romance series “Sid & Zoey.” 

	The show hails from creator Jon Kasdan and writer John Shiban. Both also serve as executive producers and co-showrunners. Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Bad Robot also executive produce. Netflix has given the show an eight-episode order. 

	The logline for the show states: 


	“Sid, a seductive, sophisticated, and amoral teenager from New York, is sent to live with a police chief and his family in the idyllic Mississippi town where his mother grew up. The family includes the chief’s sharp-witted, punk-rock daughter, Zoey. Resisting their mutual attraction, Sid and Zoey find themselves drawn into a dark, hidden world beneath the town’s picture-postcard facade — and a supernatural mystery that may well get them killed if they don’t kill each other first.” 
	

	Along with Kasdan and Shiban, J.J. Abrams and Rachel Rusch Rich executive produce for Bad Robot alongside James Wan and Rob Hackett for Blumhouse Atomic Monster. 

	Netflix has been making a concerted push into the YA space, building on the success of series like “Wednesday,” “Ginny & Georgia,” and “My Life With the Walter Boys.” Upcoming YA shows at the streamer include “The Sticks,” “The Body,” “Poser,” “Crew Girl,” and “Minimum Wage.” 

	Kasdan most recently developed the Disney+ series followup to “Willow.” He has also worked on shows like “Dawson’s Creek” and “Freaks & Geeks,” as well as films like “Solo: A Star Wars Story” and “The First Time.” Shiban previously worked on the hit Netflix crime drama “Ozark” in addition to shows like “Law & Order: Organized Crime” (on which he was showrunner), “Supernatural,” “The Vampire Diaries,” and “Breaking Bad.” 
	

	(Pictured: Jon Kasdan, John Shiban)

schema.headline: Netflix Orders YA Gothic Romance ‘Sid & Zoey,’ Blumhouse Atomic Monster and Bad Robot to Produce

title: Neil deGrasse Tyson, Neal Stephenson, Mira Lane, Rod Roddenberry to Judge XPRIZE Sci-Fi Film Competition
description:
XPRIZE announced the judges for its sci-fi film competition, which aims to inspire optimistic adaptations of a technology-enabled future.

	Neil deG
body:
XPRIZE announced the judges for its sci-fi film competition, which aims to inspire optimistic adaptations of a technology-enabled future.

	Neil deGrasse Tyson, Neal Stephenson, Mira Lane and Rod Roddenberry will preside over the competition. The panel will help select the grand prize winner, who will be named at Moonshots Live on Sept. 25 in Los Angeles.

	The Future Vision XPRIZE competition invites global filmmakers and creators to submit three-minute trailers or short films that depict hopeful future visions. Submissions close Aug. 15.
	

	The grand prize is $2.5 million in production funding to develop the concept, as well as $100K cash. Four runner-ups will receive $100K each, and 10 finalists will receive $10K. 


	Moonshots Live brings together filmmakers, builders and investors for a day of live competition and conversation. The event features pitches from Build with Gemini XPRIZE finalists, a $2 million hackathon and the Future Vision XPRIZE awards ceremony. The competition is supported in partnership with Range Media Partners and Google through their 100 ZEROS initiative.

	DeGrasse Tyson is an astrophysicist and director of the Hayden Planetarium at the American Museum of Natural History in New York City. Stephenson is a novelist whose books have shaped how the tech industry imagines its own future. He coined the term “metaverse” in 1992.

	Lane is vice president and founder of the Envisioning Studio at Google, an AI prototyping lab that explores emerging technologies. Roddenberry is CEO of Roddenberry Entertainment and The Roddenberry Foundation. He is the son of Gene Roddenberry, the famed creator of “Star Trek.”

schema.headline: Neil deGrasse Tyson, Neal Stephenson, Mira Lane, Rod Roddenberry to Judge XPRIZE Sci-Fi Film Competition

title: J. Smith-Cameron and Jefferson White Cast in Jeff Rutherford’s Sophomore Feature ‘In Our Own Sweet Way’ (EXCLUSIVE)
description: “Succession” star J. Smith-Cameron will star alongside “Yellowstone” actor Jefferson White in the upcoming independent feature film “In Our Own Swee
body:
“Succession” star J. Smith-Cameron will star alongside “Yellowstone” actor Jefferson White in the upcoming independent feature film “In Our Own Sweet Way” from director, writer, and producer Jeff Rutherford. 

	The film recently wrapped and is being produced under Rutherford’s banner Fred Senior Films, in association with Stoner Ranch Productions, Echo & Add, and Fair Oaks Entertainment.


	The official logline reads, “In the spring of 1988, two discordant neighbors keep an eye on each other as love, desperation and yearning pull them into a strange, startling harmony.”
	

	In a statement to Variety, Rutherford said, “Jefferson and J. are deservedly familiar to audiences around the country and the world. Here, they’re completely new and surprising.” He added, “It was an honor to work with them, and I’m excited for audiences to see the film and these two like they haven’t seen them before.”


	White, who is also a producer on the film, is best known for his breakout performance in the acclaimed Paramount+ series “Yellowstone” and recently wrapped Amazon/MGM’s “Ally Clark.” Next up, he’s set to appear in Lionsgate’s “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”

	Smith-Cameron, best known to audiences for her role on “Succession,” recently appeared on HBO’s “Hacks” and had a guest role on CBS’ “Elsbeth.”

	Smith-Cameron added, “‘In Our Own Sweet Way’ struck me as utterly original and imaginative from the moment I started reading it. Then I had a fabulous long talk with Jeff Rutherford and was really gratified with how intelligently he spoke about the film — he genuinely had a fresh, unique idea for it that he devoted himself to, and inspired us to devote ourselves to, as well. He and Alfonso Herrera Salcedo, the DP, had such a distinct look and tone in mind. Erin Orr who did the costumes and production designer Dan Maughiman, as well. Jefferson and I really connected – he’s a beautiful actor and a kindred spirit. I can’t wait to see it!”
	

	“The script for ‘In Our Sweet Way’ blew me away — it’s an achingly beautiful examination of love’s resilience against all odds — and I was honored to join the producing team. J. Smith-Cameron is one of my favorite actors and to work opposite her was a dream come true. Jeff Rutherford and his frequent collaborator cinematographer Alfonso Herrera Salcedo are utterly singular filmmakers, and I can’t wait to see their vision realized,” added White.

	Kyle Eaton joins Rutherford and White as producers. The film is executive produced by Alexandra Byer, Roger Mancusi, and Barry and Carmen Nordstrand. Alexander Spenser Gould is a co-producer.

	White is represented by Lichter, Grossman, Nichols, Feldman, Rogal, Shikora & Clark, INC.

	Smith-Cameron Is represented by Principal Entertainment La, Gersh, Origin Public Relations, and Schreck Rose Dapello Adams Berlin & Dunham.

schema.headline: J. Smith-Cameron and Jefferson White Cast in Jeff Rutherford’s Sophomore Feature ‘In Our Own Sweet Way’ (EXCLUSIVE)

title: ‘The Mandalorian and Grogu’ Sets Disney+ Release Date in September
description: A galaxy far, far away is about to get closer than ever. “The Mandalorian and Grogu” will be available to stream on Disney+ starting Sept. 2 after g
body:
A galaxy far, far away is about to get closer than ever. “The Mandalorian and Grogu” will be available to stream on Disney+ starting Sept. 2 after grossing $345 million worldwide in theaters this summer. That total made it the lowest grossing live-action “Star Wars” movie (below the $393 million haul of “Solo”).

	Directed by Jon Favreau, the film premiered in theaters May 22 and follows bounty hunter Din Djarin (Pedro Pascal) and his apprentice, Grogu, as they’re recruited by officer Colonel Ward (Sigourney Weaver) to aid the New Republic. The unlikely duo must rescue the heir to Jabba the Hutt, Rotta the Hutt (voiced by “The Bear’s” Jeremy Allen White), in order to track down an Imperial leader.
	

	The cast also features Martin Scorsese, who makes a guest appearance as fry cook Hugo Durant. This isn’t his first time working with the franchise, though, as the filmmaker also held a brief role in “Solo: A Star Wars Story” as cook Rio Durant.


	“The Mandalorian and Grogu” takes place after “The Mandalorian” Season 3 and “Ahsoka” Season 1, both Disney+ original series. The film cost $165 million to produce and earned $102 million through its Memorial Day weekend opening.

	Mando is voiced by Pascal, though much of the physical work is done by stunt performers Lateef Crowder and Brendan Wayne. Favreau co-wrote the film alongside Dave Filoni, who was promoted to president of Lucasfilm earlier this year following Kathleen Kennedy’s departure.

	This is the first “Star Wars” movie since “The Rise of Skywalker” in 2019, which earned $1 billion globally. Next up for the franchise is “Star Wars: Starfighter,” which will premiere May 28, 2027, and star Ryan Gosling with Shawn Levy directing.

schema.headline: ‘The Mandalorian and Grogu’ Sets Disney+ Release Date in September

title: ‘Lioness’ Season 3 Opens With 7.1 Million Viewers in Three Days, Up From Season 2 (EXCLUSIVE)
description:
The Season 3 premiere of “Lioness” hit 7.1 million viewers in its first seven days of streaming.

	That total, which comes from Paramount’s internal
body:
The Season 3 premiere of “Lioness” hit 7.1 million viewers in its first seven days of streaming.

	That total, which comes from Paramount’s internal data, puts the Aug. 2 episode significantly above the audience Season 2 reached with its debut in 2024. According to preliminary data from Nielsen, “Lioness” Season 2 was the second-most-watched streaming original series in the U.S. during the week of Aug. 2-8. It was also the No. 1 buzziest streaming drama between Aug. 2 and Aug. 4, per Social Content Ratings, drumming up 6.9 million views on social media.
	

	In addition to Paramount+, “Lioness” streams on SkyShowtime in Europe, where Season 3 also outperformed both previous seasons and is on track to land as one of the top five returning premieres ever.


	This adds to a string of strong ratings for Taylor Sheridan-produced series on Paramount+; “The Madison” hit 8 million views in 10 days in March, and “Dutton Ranch” hit 12.9 million views in seven days in May.

	“Lioness” stars Zoe Saldana and Nicole Kidman as CIA officers. Per the official logline for Season 3, “Joe (Saldaña) walks the line between duty and home as unseen forces circle her world. Patterns appear where they shouldn’t, names vanish and paths rearrange. Guided by Kaitlyn (Kidman) and Westfield (Michael Kelly), Joe confronts enemies operating in the shadows, leaving her to reckon with a war that now reaches into every part of her life.” The cast also includes Laysla De Oliveira, Genesis Rodriguez, Dave Annable, Jill Wagner, LaMonica Garrett, James Jordan, Austin Hébert, Jonah Wharton, Hannah Love Lanier, Thad Luckinbill, Ian Bohen and Morgan Freeman.  
	

	Taylor Sheridan executive produces “Lioness” with David C. Glasser, Saldaña, Kidman, Ron Burkle, David Hutkin, Bob Yari, Michael Friedman, Jill Wagner, David Lemanowicz, Geyer Kosinski and Keith Cox. Paramount Television Studios and 101 Studios produce the series.

schema.headline: ‘Lioness’ Season 3 Opens With 7.1 Million Viewers in Three Days, Up From Season 2 (EXCLUSIVE)

title: Box Office: ‘End of Oak Street’ Makes $2.5 Million in Previews
description: Dinosaur fans are in luck because two prehistoric films, “The End of Oak Street” and “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie,” are hitting theaters this weekend
body:
Dinosaur fans are in luck because two prehistoric films, “The End of Oak Street” and “Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie,” are hitting theaters this weekend, but they’ll be no match for reigning box office champion “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.”

	Warner Bros.’ “The End of Oak Street,” starring Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor as suburbanites magically transported back to prehistoric times, made $2.5 million in previews at the box office. Out of the new releases this weekend, it’s expected to come out on top with $20 million to $30 million, with Warner Bros. projecting $18 million to $23 million domestically and $20 million to $25 million internationally. With a budget above $80 million, it’ll need to ride its positive reviews and word-of-mouth to become profitable in the dog days of summer.
	

	However, Sony and Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” will still conquer the box office charts for the third week in a row. It’s estimated to bring in $65 million to $70 million this weekend, a roughly 55% decline. It’s on track to soon cross $2 billion worldwide, and after just 12 days on screens it became the year’s highest-grossing movie with $1.68 billion globally.


	“Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie” made $1.9 million in previews and is projected to make $20 million this weekend, landing it in third place. That’s a similar opening to the family-friendly show’s last film spinoff, 2023’s “The Mighty Movie,” which made $22 million and climbed to $205 million globally against a $30 million budget. “The Dino Movie” carries a slightly larger $40 million price tag, which was split between Paramount and Spin Master.
	

	Meanwhile, “The Odyssey” is aiming to add $17 million to $20 million in its fifth weekend, and a trio of new releases, “The Wrong Girls,” “The Rivals of Amziah King” and “The Brink of War,” are looking at single-digit openings.

schema.headline: Box Office: ‘End of Oak Street’ Makes $2.5 Million in Previews

	Disney fans are in for a treat this Sunday as the Mouse House unites ten of its most memorable characters and voices for “Disney Princess: The Ultimate Concert Celebration.” 

	The Wonderful World of Disney special airs Sunday, Aug. 16 at 8 p.m. on ABC and features highlights from the D23 Expo taking place this weekend at the Anaheim Convention Center next to Disneyland. 


	Night one of D23 2026 kicked off with a special concert that brought together the largest gathering of Disney princess talent ever assembled. Performers included Jodi Benson, the original voice of Ariel in Walt Disney Animation Studios’ “The Little Mermaid;” Paige O’Hara, the original voice of Belle in “Beauty and the Beast;” Auli’i Cravalho, the original voice of the titular character in “Moana” and “Moana 2;” and Brandy, who played Cinderella in the 1997 Disney made-for-TV special, “Rodgers & Hammerstein’s Cinderella.”


	The performers all performed their signature songs from their respective movies, with some being joined by special guests. Benson, for example, was joined by Halle Bailey, who played Ariel in the live-action “Little Mermaid” film. Brandy, meantime, joined Lea Salonga (the original singing voice of Jasmine in “Aladdin”) for the film’s popular duet, “A Whole New World.”

	In addition to the musical performances, the one-night-only concert is expected to showcase fireworks and light displays from Disneyland and re-visit memorable scenes from Disney princess movies through the years, beginning with 1937’s “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs” to 2024’s “Moana 2.“

            Tate, who shares kids Indy and Ocean with Taylor, filed court docs on Thursday with his request. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The move comes weeks after Tate asked the court to grant him a restraining order against Taylor due to her alleged increasingly erratic behavior. 
      

            Tate said he believed he should have sole legal and physical custody of the kids. Taylor adamantly denied his accusations. 
      
    
            A couple of weeks later, the judge ordered Taylor to submit to drug tests in the case. The court said the Mormon Wives star would have unsupervised visits with her kids, unless a drug test came back dirty … then the visits would become supervised. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            A source close to TFP tells TMZ … Taylor took a drug test and the parties agree that the results should be shared with the State. This is part of broader cooperation and transparency with the State.
      
    
            Sources close to Taylor previously told TMZ she believes her ex-boyfriend, Dakota Mortensen, is spreading lies to Tate, which caused him to rush to court. 
      
    
            Taylor is also still fighting Dakota in court over custody.

title: Surrogate McKenna West Vows Supreme Court Fight Over Baby
description:
Surrogate McKenna West's Lawyer
                          We'll Take Baby Battle to Supreme Court
body:
Surrogate McKenna West's Lawyer
                          We'll Take Baby Battle to Supreme Court!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 13, 2026
                            6:36 PM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  August 14, 2026
                                6:28 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Surrogate McKenna West is gearing up for a massive legal fight over the baby she carried ... with her attorney saying they're prepared to take the battle all the way to the U.S. Supreme Court.
      
    
            West's attorney, Lincoln Wilson, told the New York Post they're challenging a California court order giving the baby's biological parents custody, arguing West should be recognized as the mom because she gave birth in Texas.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Wilson says his side believes the California judgment is invalid and, if they don't prevail in the lower courts, “we'll take it up to the US Supreme Court if we have to.” He maintains once the California order is tossed, West is the mom under Texas law.
      

            The declaration comes just hours after we first reported West currently has no decision-making authority over the newborn.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The biological parents obtained a temporary restraining order barring West from making medical decisions for the boy, taking possession of him, representing herself as his parent or guardian, removing him from the hospital or interfering with the biological parents' access to him.
      
    
            As we reported ... West entered into a surrogacy agreement with the California couple, and the agreement included a provision allowing them to request termination if a fetal anomaly was discovered.
      
    
    
              
                
  
    
            The baby was later diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome, a serious congenital heart defect. West refused to terminate the pregnancy and traveled to Texas to give birth, setting off the legal showdown.
      
    
            The TRO remains in effect until at least August 25, when West has been ordered to appear in a Dallas court.

title: 'The Challenge' Star Tyler Duckworth Found Dead in Overflowing Bathtub
description:
'The Challenge' Tyler Duckworth
                          Found Dead in Overflowing Bathtub
body:
'The Challenge' Tyler Duckworth
                          Found Dead in Overflowing Bathtub
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 14, 2026
                            6:52 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Tyler Duckworth was found dead in an overflowing bathtub after a neighbor noticed water coming from his North Dakota apartment ... TMZ has learned.
      
    
            Grand Forks PD tells TMZ ... officers responded to "The Challenge" star's home around 11:45 AM Tuesday for a welfare check involving an unresponsive person.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Police say a maintenance worker had gone into Tyler's unit after a neighbor reported excessive water coming from the apartment ... and discovered an overflowing bathtub with Tyler's body inside.
      

            We're told officers found no outward signs of trauma -- including no gunshot or stab wounds -- and preliminary findings show no indication Tyler's death was a homicide.
      
    
            Police say the cause of death will ultimately come down to the autopsy.
      
    
            We're told an officer spoke with Tyler's mother during the investigation, but police were unable to verify any medical history.
      
    
            As we reported ... Tyler died Tuesday at 44. His death was initially classified as unattended, meaning no one witnessed it.
      
    
            Tyler was best known for his lengthy run on MTV's "The Challenge," winning "Cutthroat" in 2010 and "Rivals" in 2011. He first entered the MTV universe on "The Real World: Key West" in 2006 and later returned to the 'Challenge' franchise for 'All Stars.'
      
    
            He made his final public appearance less than two weeks before his death at a "Challenge Mania" event in Minneapolis on July 31.

title: Taylor Frankie Paul Shares Petition Demanding Release of Her 'Bachelorette' Season
description:
Taylor Frankie Paul
                          Look How Many Fans Want to See My 'Bachelorette' Se
body:
Taylor Frankie Paul
                          Look How Many Fans Want to See My 'Bachelorette' Season!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 14, 2026
                            9:16 AM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Taylor Frankie Paul's still holding out hope fans might see her fall in love on "The Bachelorette" ... sharing a petition that calls for ABC to air the dang thing ... and it's got a lot of signatures.
      
    
            The reality star posted the link to her Instagram story ... telling her fans she loved them for making it -- and admitting she signed it herself.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Taylor also shared the full demand letter from the petition ... which argues fans have been deprived of watching the star on a once-in-a-lifetime journey. Her fans say they've followed her and "know her heart."
      

            The petition goes on to say taking away the season doesn't solve an issue -- it only silences TFP ... and viewers should be allowed to watch the show and form their own opinions of the star.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As of this morning, the petition has more than 16,000 signatures ... though it'll need a whole lot more to change the mind of ABC execs ... who opted not to run the season when it was supposed to air back in March.
      
    
            Of course, the season was pulled after we published video of Taylor throwing a barstool at her ex, Dakota Mortensen, with her kid in the room. Taylor's been engaged in a custody battle with Dakota and her other ex, Tate Paul, in the months since the video came out.
      
    
      
        
              
    
    
            Production sources told us "The Bachelorette" season was supposed to run starting in July ... but it didn't happen.
      
    
            Instead, Utah's Department of Children and Family Services asked a juvenile court to find that Taylor's three children have been "abused, neglected or dependent."
